## Natural history notes

A large water scavenger beetle characterized by a smooth oval black to dark brown body, short clubbed antennae, and flattened swimming legs. In Florida, Hydrophilus ovatus is found in ponds, marshes, ditches, canals, wetlands, and slow vegetated waters, with Florida included in its eastern North American range. Adults are mostly aquatic scavengers and omnivores that feed on decaying plant material, algae, detritus, and small aquatic organisms, while the larvae are more predatory and use strong jaws to capture other aquatic invertebrates.
